pairs.why: B is built like the real chair: a slim tube frame, a rectangular sling backrest and crossed X legs. A is a padded armchair with toy-like lime trim, which is a different and more toy-looking object.
Both match the real chair's frame, but in B the seat and back fabric wrap around the tubes as sleeves, like the real card, so it reads as a better-built object than A's flat seat.
A hangs on the striped wall with a soft drop shadow and a rounded rim, like the real clock. B stands on a floor ledge and looks flatter and more like a graphic.
The two are nearly identical wall clocks. B's rim is slightly deeper orange with a clearer side shadow, which is a bit closer to the real card, but the difference is marginal.
A is wall-mounted with a soft cast shadow and a moderately glossy rim, like the real card. B is a free-standing clock on a floor with flatter, crisper rendering.
A matches the real clock's wall-hung setup and rounded, softly lit rim. B stands on the ground and looks more like a flat vector.
A sits flush on the wall with a soft shadow, like the real clock. B is placed on a floor plane, and its rim and face read flatter.
B adds a red center pin, but it still stands on a floor with flatter shading. A keeps the real card's wall-hung look and its soft, rounded glossy rim.
